# Scheduled atomic capture, long retention, and sparse physical-port errors
30 October 2026. New synthesis and soft-phase proof. V2 local working theorem awaiting independent whole-source review. The binding same-envelope refinement is TWO_PARAMETER_MOMENT_FAMILY.md; V1 is preserved as a rejected incomplete draft. It does not claim a quantum factory or native two-site implementation.

## 1. Exact contract
There are arbitrarily many records with genuine classical instrument outcomes m_j. Conditional on the full m vector, each physical raw bit starts in |m_j> and DATA/bath can depend arbitrarily on m. Raw latches are noisy thereafter. Target bits can start arbitrarily dirty and correlated. The fixed-size noisy seed/reset/copy contract and its joint bounds are those in GENUINE_CLASSICAL_SEED_RECEIVING.md plus SEED_MIXED_RESET_SUBSET_LEMMA.md.

Use the literal nested bounded-degree expander prefixes, strict external-edge-energy majority primitives, fixed physical root ports, and scheduled soft-reset/sharpen/copy stages in the reviewed source bundle. The atomic majority dissipators have fixed body d+1, fixed rates and bounded per-site incidence; d and rates may be enormous constants. This is the declared physical resource, not a two-site compilation. Capture needs O(log n) scheduled stages and O(n) sites/site-time per record. The final graph remains on autonomously for a prescribed retention horizon H.

Actual perturbations have the existing bounded-q system-leg, per-site incident-cb, identity-annihilating, normal joint-system/bath contract, and the TOTAL actual evolution is CPTP. Arbitrary common-bath correlations and distant bounded-number legs are allowed. No independence, Pauli trajectory or positive signed-fault expansion is assumed. A bounded number of actual quantum read couplings may use each root as a Z-diagonal control. These commute all classical diagonal tests; arbitrary retained DATA does not change the classical theorem. It DOES NOT follow that the quantum DATA remains correct.

The conclusion concerns the actual simultaneous computational-basis error observables at physical root ports, relative to the historical m. A separate final detector is not assumed perfect. No classical analysis reference is a physical protected register.

# Two-parameter same-envelope norm: the growth-to-soft-retention correction
30 October 2026. Binding refinement of POSITIVE_BLOCK_MOMENT_RECEIVING.md. This corrects a real insufficiency in the first retention draft. Local proof awaiting review.

## The rejected shortcut
A signed component controlled only with F=e^(sU) can have norm exp(rho_g n). From that bound alone, G=1+e^(-alpha n)F costs exp(rho_g n), not 1+exp[-(alpha-rho_g)n]. A separate small root-only moment estimate with DIFFERENT positive envelopes is insufficient. The old V1 draft is preserved under failed_drafts and must not be used alone.

## 1. Both subset indices are retained
For current remaining records R, use all pairs B,A subset R:

 H_(B,A)(t)=(product_(j in B)phi_j(t))(product_(j in A)Z_j(t)),
 W_(B,A)(t)=(product_(j in B)w_j(t)) M^|A|.

Here phi_j>=I is the actual phase metric, first the growth exponential F_j and later the softened G_j. The positive scalar w_j is its normalization budget; it need not equal a physical moment. Define the norm by ONE pair of positive diagonal envelopes Y_L,Y_R in a positive 2-by-2 block with off-diagonal X, requiring

 Tr(H_(B,A)Y_L,R)<=C W_(B,A) for EVERY B,A.             (D1)

The B=A=empty condition makes this a definite norm dominating trace norm, even if some normalized tests are <I. All reference-stabilized statements use the same definition. This is a finite norm family, not an exponential-size physical procedure.

## 2. Intervals and growth endpoints
For EVERY phase subset B, the actual phase/root drift has its phase source sum_(j in B)a_j(t) and the same coefficientwise root hierarchy indexed by A. Set w'_j=a_j w_j. Divide the corresponding complete operator comparisons by product_B w_j. The root affine comparison has normalized row sum<=1 whenever z_*j<=M. Applying the SAME actual CP map to Y_L,Y_R proves contraction in (D1), simultaneously for every pair B,A.

A soft-target attachment multiplies a selected phase factor by at most exp(epsilon_init L_new), while its rooted pullback is nonincreasing; multiply that w_j by this declared factor. The actual PRE-to-POST endpoint has phi'_j<=phi_j after pullback and similarly for all rooted subsets. Good-cut maps contract. Graph/copy endpoints and moving charts are the reviewed ones; no new physical operation is introduced.

During growth, w_j<=w_seed exp(rho_g n_j), using actual geometric prefix size.
